description.narrative:
The Sustainable Avocado Productivity (SAP) Project is a five-year initiative running from 2025 to 2028 aimed at improving the livelihoods of smallholder avocado farmers—women, men, and youth—in Murang'a County. Its core objective is to increase productivity and incomes for these farmers by 2028. To achieve this, the project focuses on strengthening governance and gender-responsive services, building advocacy capacity, and expanding access to financial and insurance services. It also aims to enhance farmer resilience, empower women and youth through transformative actions, increase the production and diversity of nutritious foods, and improve post-harvest handling, value addition, and market access. Implementation will take place across eight sub-counties through 17 registered avocado cooperative societies. Activities will target three levels: individual farmers, to improve farming skills; primary cooperatives; and the union level, to strengthen leadership, governance, and service delivery. The project directly targets 3,218 men, 1,230 women, and 512 young people, while indirectly benefiting 16,681 household members through spill-over effects.
A key ambition of the project is to help the union access international avocado markets and develop processing capacities. These efforts aim to raise fruit value, increase farmer income, and strengthen the long-term financial sustainability of cooperatives and project outcomes.
